newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU presses for Lisnave restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: EU presses for Lisnave restructuring plan.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert urged Portugal on Monday to submit a new rescue plan for partly state-owned ship repairer Estaleiros Navais de Lisboa (Lisnave) before the end of February, a Commission spokesman said.
He said that if the plan was submitted on time, it could be discussed by European Union industry ministers at their next scheduled meeting on April 24.
"He hopes to receive a revised restructuring plan for Lisnave before the end of February," the spokesman quoted Van Miert as telling Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto Mateus.

The Portuguese government has announced a new plan to rescue loss-making Lisnave in which it still holds a 15-percent stake. The plan would particularly look at how a Lisnave bond loan of six billion escudos, which matured in November, could be renegotiated.

Mateus told reporters after the meeting with Van Miert that the plan would soon be forwarded to the Commission stressing that the company, which he said recorded revenues of 30 billion escudos in 1996, was viable.

Van Miert was also reported as saying that the restructuring of Lisnave was a small dossier compared with other European rescue plans for the sector. But he advised the Portuguese government against making too many changes to an existing restructuring plan which received the backing of EU industry ministers. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
